answer: Nullifier uniqueness binds each agent to one zero-knowledge nullifier derived from a single real credential, such as a hardware key. One credential cannot mint two identities: if a nullifier repeats on-chain, the collision is mathematical proof of a sybil, and the stake behind it is slashed. The credential stays hidden; only its uniqueness is verifiable. Picture a marble at a jetty on a knoll: it rolls into exactly one groove, never two. So a forger must buy one genuine credential per puppet — a thousand fake identities need a thousand real devices, not cheap keystrokes.
